question: Sam drove \(96\) miles in \(90\) minutes. His average speed during the first \(30\) minutes was \(60\) mph (miles per hour), and his average speed during the second \(30\) minutes was \(65\) mph. What was his average speed, in mph, during the last \(30\) minutes?
solution:
Each \(30\)-minute interval is \(\tfrac12\) hour, so we can first find the distances Sam drove in the first two intervals. Using distance equals speed times time, these are
\[
60\cdot\frac12=30\text{ miles},\qquad
65\cdot\frac12=32.5\text{ miles}.
\]
The distance left for the last interval is therefore
\[
96-30-32.5=33.5\text{ miles}.
\]
His average speed during that half hour was
\[
\frac{33.5}{1/2}=\boxed{67}\text{ mph},
\]
choice \(\text{(D)}\).
